name: Archetype: small modern militaries, territorial and total defence

weightNotes.aggression: Doctrine is to deter, delay and hold until allies arrive (RAND RR-2779 on Baltic total defence: 'buy time for' national and NATO conventional responses). Counterattacks only locally.
weightNotes.maneuver: Small mechanised cores (often one or two brigades) plus large territorial forces; defence-oriented positional fighting with local mobile counterattacks. Below middle.
weightNotes.flanking: Home-terrain knowledge favours ambush and raids on enemy flanks and columns (Ukrainian territorial units north of Kyiv, 2022), but formations are too small for operational envelopment.
weightNotes.siegePreference: Defends its own cities rather than seeking enemy ones; objective scoring should favour own threatened cities. Low.
weightNotes.reserveUse: Mobilised reservists and national guard (Estonian Defence League, Latvian national guard, RAND RR-2779) form a sizeable second line; middling.
weightNotes.scouting: Excellent local knowledge, civilian reporting networks and cheap drones; limited strategic ISR without allies. Middling.
weightNotes.retreatThreshold: Basis: share of starting strength lost (killed, wounded, captured, missing) at the moment of withdrawal or break, never the battle total with pursuit. derived:breakpoint-quartile: modelRules.breakpoint.loserCasualtyShareAtBreak.modern low quartile 0.04. Sourced early withdrawal: delay doctrine trades space for time and pulls forces back to cities and forests for resistance (RAND RR2779; RAND RR1253 on Baltic defence collapsing within 60 hours). No measured share.
weightNotes.combinedArms: Modern but thin: anti-tank missiles, mortars, some artillery and air defence; little or no air force. Middling.
weightNotes.initiative: Small professional cadres and reservists trained for decentralised resistance (RAND RR-2779 on unconventional warfare and resistance); Nordic and Baltic forces use mission command. Educated judgement.
weightNotes.logisticsDiscipline: Fights on interior lines inside its own supply network with prepositioned caches; operations rarely leave home territory. High.

summary: Small states (Baltic and Nordic states, Switzerland, Singapore-style conscript forces, Georgia, Taiwan in its newer concepts) that cannot match a great-power neighbour. They combine a small professional or conscript core with mass reservists, territorial defence units and whole-of-society 'total defence': delay on prepared positions and obstacles, fight from cities and forests, keep resistance going behind enemy lines, and hold long enough for allies to intervene.
whyItWorked: Raises the cost and time of invasion: RAND RR-2779 finds total defence and unconventional warfare improve warning, augment initial defences and buy time for NATO. Ukraine 2022 showed a defender that dispersed its forces and used massed fires from two artillery brigades blunting a force with a 12:1 local advantage on the approaches to Kyiv (RUSI Preliminary Lessons).
whereItFailed: Alone, against a major power, it cannot hold territory: RAND's 2014-15 wargames had Russian forces reach the outskirts of Tallinn and/or Riga within 60 hours at most (RR-1253), and RAND RR-2779 frames total defence as a complement to conventional national and NATO defence, not a substitute for it. Georgia 2008 lost its conventional battle within five days.

sources.title: RAND, Deterring Russian Aggression in the Baltic States Through Resilience and Resistance (RR-2779)
RAND, Reinforcing Deterrence on NATO's Eastern Flank: Wargaming the Defense of the Baltics (RR-1253)
RUSI, Preliminary Lessons in Conventional Warfighting from Russia's Invasion of Ukraine: February-July 2022
